messages:
morgan (support): heads up — Customer ACME reported a sharp p95/p99 jump for their Dedicated pool around 17:02 UTC. They see 3-5s p95 and 10-18s p99 for normal chat completions. They say it started after a traffic surge and persisted ~20 minutes. attaching the support repro and sample logs they sent.

ravi (eng-runtime): thanks. do we have an incident alert id?

deploy-bot: alert triggered: dedicated-pool-attach-latency-high (id: alert-2024-06-29-562) — 17:01:34 UTC — severity: high

jamie (eng-sre): quick summary from the alert: scale-up started at 17:00:58, new GPU instances provisioning completed by 17:01:45 but attach/warmup handshake stalled. lots of attach timeouts and retries. looks like a thundering-herd where many attaches coincided with customer burst.

morgan (support): customer reports their client retried 5x before success. their telemetry shows backoff retries but perceived latency is huge. they want mitigation asap (they're on Dedicated pool id dp-acme-3).

ravi (eng-runtime): can you paste the customer's request header & model? Also which model variant — quantized or fp16? that affects warmup time.

morgan (support): pasted from ACME: model: redwood-large-v1-fp16, seq len typical 512, streaming disabled. header: x-customer-id: acme-123; route: /v1/complete-dedicated; token: <redacted>

luis (infra): looking at cloud logs — nodes for dp-acme-3 were created in batch at 17:00:50. Kube pods scheduled, but gds_attach (our attach agent) reported exponential backoff due to KV cache attach race:

```
2024-06-29T17:01:10Z gds_attach error: failed to attach kvstore: timeout after 10s
2024-06-29T17:01:20Z gds_attach warn: retrying attach (attempt 3)
2024-06-29T17:01:40Z gds_attach info: attach succeeded after 4 retries
```
This matches the customer retry pattern.

anna (prodops): any chance the scheduled prewarm config was zero? If the pool was scaled down to zero, warmups will be long. What's the pool autoscale cooldown and min-size?

jamie (eng-sre): dp-acme-3 autoscale config shows min_replicas=0, burst_capacity enabled, scale_up_policy=aggressive but with attach_parallelism limited to 8. We probably hit attach_parallelism bottleneck when 200 requests hit at once.

ravi (eng-runtime): aha — parallel attach limit + min_replicas=0 = cold start storm. two mitigations: 1) bump min_replicas to 1 (or small floor) for Dedicated buckets serving production. 2) increase attach_parallelism for that pool to 64 temporarily and enable staggered attach with jitter. Also we can tweak gds_attach backoff to start shorter then ramp.

morgan (support): customer needs short-term fix — can we move them to a warm host or spin a small reserve?

luis (infra): created an emergency warm host: moved dp-acme-3 traffic to dp-acme-3-reserve with min_replicas=2. propagation started at 17:05. early telemetry shows p95 dropped to ~850ms within two minutes.

jamie (eng-sre): good. follow-up actions:
- immediate: keep reserve active for 24h, monitor p99 and attach errors.
- near-term: set min_replicas=1 for all Dedicated pools tagged production.
- medium: increase attach_parallelism threshold and add jittered attach start to gds_attach.
- long-term: implement coordinated prewarm for predicted bursts using request rate forecasts (redwood-optimize hint).

ravi (eng-runtime): I'll open a runtime PR with the attach_parallelism change + config flag. also adding a hot-start feature that maintains a soft warm cache for last N models used by the pool.

anna (prodops): I'll roll the min_replicas config change as a feature flag rollout — start with a small cohort of customers, monitor cost impact.

morgan (support): ACME confirmed improved UX and thanked us. they want a postmortem and root cause.

jamie (eng-sre): I'll author a short postmortem draft: cause = min_replicas=0 + attach_parallelism throttling + sudden customer traffic spike => thundering herd on KV attach path. mitigation = reserve warm hosts, config defaults for prod pools, runtime attach improvements. will attach logs and timeline.

ravi (eng-runtime): repro steps recorded for the postmortem:
1) create a Dedicated pool with min_replicas=0 and attach_parallelism=8.
2) send concurrent 200 start requests (seq len 512) in a <60s window to the pool.
3) observe attach retries on server logs and client latency/backoff.
4) apply warm host and verify p95/p99 improvement.

morgan (support): adding customer's repro (anonymized) and their logs to the postmortem.

luis (infra): follow-ups for infra: add metrics for per-pool attach queue length and per-node gds_attach_latency histogram. also add alert for attach_retries > 50 per minute.

anna (prodops): schedule a config rollout and cost/benefit analysis for default min_replicas=1 for prod.

jamie (eng-sre): tagging internal owners: @ravi please own runtime PR, @luis infra metrics, @anna rollout, @morgan customer comms. I'll write the postmortem and link to the incident alert.

morgan (support): thanks all. closing thread once postmortem posted. :white_check_mark:
